summary: Montana lookout rebuilt three times since c.1920; now a rentable cab atop a shared radio tower in the Lolo National Forest.

facts.design: live-in cab on concrete tower base (resembles an air-traffic-control tower)
facts.status_note: not regularly staffed for fire detection in recent years; building shared with active communications equipment

access.note: available as a paid overnight rental via Recreation.gov; entry gate and lookout kept locked, access code sent with reservation

visit.trail_note: reached via Forest Service roads from Superior, MT; high-clearance driving, not a hike-in

events.note: first used about 1920 as a tree platform tower
30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab replaced the tree platform
present 20-foot concrete base with live-in cab replaced the pole tower after bear and vandalism damage

evidence.supports: built c.1920 as tree platform, 1934 pole/L-4, 1984 concrete tower resembling an aircraft control tower; bear and vandal damage; staffing names
evidence.quote: First used about 1920 with a tree platform tower, a 30' pole tower with L-4 cab replaced it in 1934. After having survived bears eating up the tower legs, and vandals taking chainsaws to it, the tower was replaced in 1984 with the present 20' concrete base topped with a live-in cab which makes it resemble an aircraft control tower.

evidence.supports: staff names and years, not regularly staffed, rental availability
evidence.quote: It has not been regularly staffed for several years. The lookout is currently available on the Recreation Rental program. Known lookout personnel: 1950, 1954: Fern Bonnell; 1953: Garry O'Hara; 1957-1959: Katherine Mercer.

evidence.supports: shared radio/cellular tower, third-floor cab, concrete construction
evidence.quote: The lookout is located on the third floor of a multiple story building that is used as a radio and cellular tower. Equipment is located on other floors of the building. It is constructed out of concrete blocks with an enclosed stairway, making it more suitable for children.

evidence.supports: locked access, max occupancy, directions, repair crews on lower floors
evidence.quote: This Lookout is a shared site with active communications on the first and second floors. Be advised that in emergencies, workers may be utilizing the first and second floors for repairs during your stay.

sources.title: Thompson Peak Lookout Tower, Lolo National Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief lists design as L-4 and status 'standing', consistent with sources, but the 1920/1934/1984 structure history (tree platform -> pole/L-4 -> concrete) is richer than the brief's single '1920 built' event; consider adding the 1934 and 1984 events to the record. No NHLR/NRHP source was checked for this tower in this pass; firelookout.org listing only confirmed location/name match.
